# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Old Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches; the old system remains fully operational as a fallback until all users are confirmed stable on the new system, and for a defined stabilization window afterward.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (1% of users — 400 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full parallel-run reconciliation testing against the old system for at least 2 consecutive weeks with zero unresolved discrepancies in invoice totals, tax calculation, and payment posting; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end in staging.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk customers (no active disputes, standard payment methods, month-to-month plans).

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum.

**Exit criteria to advance:** Billing accuracy ≥ 99.95% (invoice value matches old-system shadow calculation), no P1/P2 incidents open, support ticket volume for billing issues within 1.5x baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users — 10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Engineering and Finance leads; automated dual-write reconciliation job deployed and running hourly with alerting configured.

**Scope:** Broader mix of customer segments (varied plan types, geographies, payment methods), excluding enterprise/high-ARR accounts.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, migrated in weekly sub-batches (e.g., ~2,500/week) to allow monitoring between increments.

**Exit criteria to advance:** Payment failure rate on migrated cohort within 0.2 percentage points of old-system baseline; reconciliation discrepancies resolved within 24 hours each; no unresolved data-integrity incidents.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (74% of users — remaining ~29,600 users, including enterprise/high-ARR accounts last)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; enterprise account managers briefed and customer-specific migration windows scheduled for top-tier accounts; finance close process validated on new system for one full billing cycle.

**Scope:** All remaining users, with enterprise/high-touch accounts migrated in the final sub-batch under white-glove monitoring.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks, in progressively larger weekly sub-batches.

**Exit criteria to advance:** 100% of active users migrated and confirmed generating accurate invoices for at least one full billing cycle on the new system.

---

## Post-Migration Stabilization Phase (0% additional user migration — parallel-run wind-down)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 exit criteria met; all 40,000 users have completed at least one full billing cycle on the new system with no open critical discrepancies.

**Scope:** No further user migration occurs in this phase. Both systems continue running in parallel (old system in read-only/standby mode) for a minimum of one additional full billing cycle to confirm stability, support any late-arriving disputes or adjustments, and complete final financial reconciliation. Decommissioning of the old billing system is planned only after this phase concludes successfully and is treated as a separate, subsequent initiative — not part of the final user migration batch.

---

## Key Metrics and Halt Threshold

Rollout is automatically halted (no further batches migrated) if any of the following occur:

- **Billing accuracy drops below 99.5%** (invoice discrepancy rate on migrated cohort exceeds 0.5%) — HALT and roll back the affected batch.
- Payment failure rate on migrated cohort exceeds baseline by more than 1 percentage point for any 24-hour window.
- More than 5 P1 incidents attributable to the new billing system occur within any single phase.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing of customers due to both systems processing the same invoice | Implement idempotency keys and a hard cutover flag per account so only one system is authoritative for billing at any time | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems during parallel run causes reconciliation to silently diverge | Run automated hourly reconciliation jobs with alerting and require sign-off before each phase advance | Data Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers experience invoice errors that damage trust and revenue relationships | Migrate enterprise accounts last, in small sub-batches, with dedicated account manager monitoring and 48-hour white-glove support | Customer Success Lead
RISK: Rollback of a migrated batch is not actually feasible once payment methods are re-tokenized in the new system | Test full rollback procedure in staging before Phase 1 and require a validated rollback runbook as an entry criterion for every phase | Platform Reliability Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during migration spikes | Staff a dedicated migration support queue and cap weekly batch size to match support capacity | Support Operations Lead

PHASES: 4
